title: Trip Job Scheduler
description: Distributed job scheduler: fire-lag SLO, runs/outcomes, claims and partitions, leases, tenant fairness, notification sink, JVM/HikariCP/caches.

panels.title: Fire-lag p99 (SLO 2 s)
panels.description: p99 of (actual fire time - scheduled fire time) across selected nodes. SLO: p99 < 2 s. Red means the SLO is breached; check claim latency, DB pool and tenant caps.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Runs due now but not yet claimed (cluster-wide DB count; every node reports the same value, so max is used). Sustained growth means claim throughput is too low.

panels.title: Running
panels.description: Runs currently in state running (cluster-wide DB count).

panels.title: Retrying
panels.description: Runs waiting for a retry after a retryable failure or timeout (cluster-wide).

panels.title: Dead-lettered
panels.description: Runs that exhausted retries or failed permanently. Any value above 0 needs human triage.

panels.title: Error rate (5m)
panels.description: Share of run outcomes that were not success (retryable + permanent + timeout) over the last 5 minutes. Red above 5 %.

panels.title: Stale commits (1h)
panels.description: Commits rejected because the run's lease epoch was stale (another node took it over). Non-zero indicates lease loss or GC pauses; exactly-once is still preserved by fencing.

panels.title: Fire lag p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Fire-lag quantiles across selected nodes. Dashed red line is the 2 s p99 SLO.

panels.title: Fire lag distribution
panels.description: Heatmap of fire-lag histogram buckets. A band drifting upward means lag is growing for a share of runs.

panels.title: Fire lag p99 by handler
panels.description: p99 fire lag broken down by job handler; isolates a single slow handler type.

panels.title: Fire lag p99 by tenant tier
panels.description: p99 fire lag per tenant tier; a single tier above SLO suggests a fairness or cap problem.

panels.title: Runs by state and queue depth
panels.description: Cluster-wide run counts per state plus due-but-unclaimed queue depth (max across nodes, since every node reports the same DB count).

panels.title: Outcomes rate
panels.description: Run completions per second by outcome across selected nodes.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Non-success outcomes / all outcomes (5m window). Red line marks the 5 % alert threshold.

panels.title: Claim batch latency
panels.description: Time to claim one batch of due runs (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + update). Red line: 100 ms target.

panels.title: Partitions owned per node
panels.description: Partitions currently owned by each node. The total series must always equal 128; less means unowned partitions (runs will not fire), more means double ownership.

panels.title: Total partitions
panels.description: Sum of partitions owned across all nodes. Green only when exactly 128.

panels.title: Lease renew failures
panels.description: Failed partition lease renewals per second per node. Sustained failures precede lease loss.

panels.title: Lease lost by reason
panels.description: Leases lost per interval: stale_409 (renew rejected), fenced_write_0_rows (fenced write affected no rows), self_fence (node fenced itself after missed renewals).

panels.title: Orphan takeovers
panels.description: Partitions/runs taken over from dead or fenced owners per interval. Spikes accompany node crashes or rebalances.

panels.title: Orphan takeover time p99
panels.description: Time from the dead owner's last successful lease renewal (the last moment it was proven alive) to the restart by a survivor, DB clock. Normally 10-10.7 s (10 s lease + 0.5 s sweep + claim). Red line: 11.2 s alert threshold.

panels.title: Dead letters by error code
panels.description: Runs dead-lettered per interval, by error code. FENCING_CONFLICT (20 lost leases) fires SchedulerFencingConflictDeadLetters; replay from the API after fixing the cause.

panels.title: Tenant cap: configured vs effective
panels.description: Per-tenant concurrency cap as configured and as currently enforced (effective may be lowered under load). Cluster-wide value, max across nodes.

panels.title: Tenant cap rejections
panels.description: Claims skipped per second because the tenant hit its cap. A single tenant dominating here is being throttled for fairness.

panels.title: Sink deliveries by outcome
panels.description: Delivery attempts per second at the notification sink. ALREADY_DELIVERED = idempotent duplicate absorbed; STALE_TOKEN = fenced stale writer rejected; INJECTED_FAULT = chaos testing.

panels.title: Sink delivery latency
panels.description: Sink-side delivery latency quantiles.

panels.title: Heap used vs max
panels.description: JVM heap used and max per node. Used approaching max causes long GC pauses and lease loss.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Seconds per second spent in GC pauses per node (left) and pauses per second. Long pauses can exceed the lease TTL.

panels.title: Live threads
panels.description: Live JVM threads per node.

panels.title: Process CPU
panels.description: Process CPU usage per node (0-1 of available cores).

panels.title: HikariCP connections
panels.description: DB pool connections per node: active, idle, pending (threads waiting) and max. Pending > 0 for long means pool exhaustion.

panels.title: HikariCP acquire time (avg)
panels.description: Average time to acquire a DB connection per node. Rising values precede claim latency and fire-lag regressions.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Hits / gets per cache across selected nodes. A drop means more DB reads (e.g. tenant cap or job definition lookups).

panels.title: Cache size
panels.description: Entries per cache per node.
